name: King Black Dragon

mechanics.name: Dragonfire
mechanics.description: His ordinary dragonfire, thrown at whoever he is facing. Unprotected it is the biggest hit in the lair.
mechanics.counterplay: Bring an antifire and a dragonfire shield. One without the other still leaves a large hit.

mechanics.name: Poison Breath
mechanics.description: A green breath from the left head that poisons on top of the damage.
mechanics.counterplay: An antifire does not stop the poison. Bring an antipoison as well.

mechanics.name: Ice Breath
mechanics.description: A white breath from the right head that freezes you where you stand.
mechanics.counterplay: Break the freeze or wait it out with your antifire up. Being frozen is what stacks the damage.

mechanics.name: Lightning Breath
mechanics.description: A blue breath from the middle head that drains your stats as it lands.
mechanics.counterplay: Restore afterwards rather than fighting on drained. The drain is the lasting part.

_note: SKELETON, NOT LIVE-VERIFIED. Ids come from Jagex's own gameval names rather than guesses, but nothing here has been confirmed in a live fight. Provenance: gamevals from runelite-api 1.12.35 (net.runelite.api.gameval.*), because this cache download ships an empty GAMEVALS index (idx24) and ScanGameVal cannot read it; npc names, models, sequences and extents from the live cache (revision of 2026-08-06). Npc ids 239 and 2642, the second being a recoloured cutscene copy (TWOCATS_KBD_CUTSCENE) that shares the model set and animations. KBD_PET 6636 and POH_KBD_PET 6652 are excluded. THIS BOSS HAS NO ANIMATIONS OF ITS OWN. Npc 239's standing animation is 90, which the gamevals name DRAGON_READY, so it reuses the generic dragon set wholesale: DRAGON_BLOCK 89, DRAGON_HEAD_ATTACK 91, DRAGON_DEATH 92. That set has exactly one attack sequence, DRAGON_HEAD_ATTACK 91, which is why the three mechanics here cannot each have their own animation. Because the animations are generic, the animation trigger is doing real work: an animation only matches when played by an npc the engine is currently tracking as this boss (docs/DECISIONS.md D17), so an ordinary dragon nearby cannot false-positive. THE THREE MECHANICS ARE SPLIT BY COUNTERPLAY, NOT BY TRIGGER, AND TWO OF THE THREE TRIGGERS ARE COMPROMISES. Ordinary dragonfire takes DRAGON_HEAD_ATTACK 91 because it is the attack he throws most. The melee bite takes DRAGON_BLOCK 89, which is a defend rather than an attack sequence and is the weakest mapping in the file, chosen because it is the only other sequence in the set and because a melee bite is the only mechanic that happens exclusively at close range. The coloured breaths take a bare npc-spawn, so they unlock on arrival rather than on the breath: they are the same head attack with a different spotanim, and the cache names no KBD spotanim to tell them apart. Splitting them out anyway is deliberate, because the counterplay genuinely differs, an antifire covers the ordinary breath and does nothing against the other three, and a player reading this list needs that separated. THREE MECHANICS IS ON THE THIN SIDE and reflects how little of this boss the cache describes, not the wiki's account of it. staticFallback is false on all three; whether each body animation reads has not been eyeballed in game. The collection log page is titled 'King Black Dragon', matching 'name'. BATCH 4 2026-08-07: Bite is dropped and the single Coloured Breath row becomes three, as asked. THE THREE BREATH ROWS ARE THE UNCERTAIN PART. All three share animation 90, so they are separated by graphic instead: POISONBREATH 953, FROSTBREATH_ATTACK 3472 and BLUE_BREATH 3038, mapped to poison, ice and lightning by name. That mapping is a judgement call, and if two of them are wrong the rows will unlock as the wrong mechanic rather than not at all, which is worse. Verify with the trigger log before trusting these three. Ordinary dragonfire keeps animation 91 and is solid.
